body:
# Repair qualification backend: same maintained086 for both engines

Use already qualified0866265bd6f3d73ad572f31dc1bb954f308ed9a5d857efa9414d37e1ade13374 explicitly for BOTH JIT/interp;140e remains interpreter-origin-only and is not this repair cohort. Freeze this selection before new consumer code. Original source/journal captures remain the cause evidence; no new origin observer is needed.

Prepare a maximum four-process matched cohort: newcontrol/interp, candidate/interp, newcontrol/JIT, candidate/JIT, same original module/client/ROM/history/request20 and original45s-or6e9/15sjoin bounds. Per-arm actual firmware pins will arrive after root build. An expected original control's bounded null-fallback failure is a diagnostic observation, never a product pass; other unexpected source/protocol/status/teardown failures stop the remaining cohort. Candidates require actual restored11, three fresh decoded frames, ordinary readback, retained module state and normal FINI/unload, no unexpected memory events. Report exact heap success/failure separately; never waive a leak to manufacture a pass.

Include one ordinary successful mode transition in each candidate after the original-history refusal/retained-state/FINI checks, using a documented already supported low-memory mode, then restore11. This keeps the primary reproduction prefix unchanged; control failure naturally leaves that later control unrun. Explain exact order in your frozenplan rather than introducing a fifthprocess. No native RENDER is needed in an unsupported display format.

This is source/host preparation only. No new profile/staging/request/target until candidateclosure and later release. Normal owned teardown, freshinspection and central release precede analysis. No physical/default/publish authorization.
